title: Boxing & Kickboxing Gym Software: Packs & Drop-Ins (2026)
description: Boxing and kickboxing gym software compared: class packs, drop-ins, intro offers, bag caps, PT sessions and who counts as active. 9 tools, real prices.
body:
A fitness boxing or kickboxing studio sells differently from a belt-based martial arts school. Many customers never sign a monthly contract. They buy a drop-in, a 10-class pack or an intro week, come for a while, and maybe convert to unlimited. Classes fill up by bag count, coaches sell 1:1 pad work, and the front desk sells gloves and wraps. So the questions that matter are: can the software sell packs and drop-ins online, can it stop people from buying the free intro offer twice, can it cap a class at the number of bags, and does every drop-in customer push you into a higher price tier?

This page compares what nine vendors publish on those points. We checked each vendor's own pricing, feature and help pages on November 28, 2026. We haven't used these tools ourselves and we don't publish ratings. Anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown. Prices are in US dollars and are software fees only; card processing is extra. If you run a fight team with ranks and sparring classes, see Muay Thai gym software or MMA gym software, which cover the martial-arts-school tools in more depth. More options are on our BJJ and MMA software page.

What a boxing or kickboxing studio needs

  • Drop-ins, class packs and passes, sold online and at the desk, counted down at check-in and expiring on a date you choose.
  • Intro offers that can only be bought once, so the free first class stays a one-time offer.
  • Class caps by bag or station count, with a waitlist. Some tools also let members pick a specific spot.
  • Personal training and pad sessions booked against a coach's calendar, sold singly or in packages.
  • Retail for gloves, wraps and drinks.
  • A price you can predict. Some tools charge by active members or customers, and their definitions decide whether a busy month of drop-ins raises your bill.

Will drop-in customers raise your bill?

Three of these tools price by how many people are active, and each counts differently. Here is what the vendors say:

  • Gymdesk: visitors, frozen or cancelled members and prospects are not counted. Visitors can hold trial memberships. Gymdesk's pages don't say whether someone holding a class-pack membership is counted, so ask.
  • Zen Planner: an Active Member is anyone with a membership or who attended an event in the past month. Prospects and staff are never counted.
  • TeamUp: an active customer is anyone who had a registration or bought something during the month, counted once.

PushPress, Wodify, RhinoFit Standard, Spark and Mindbody don't price by member count (PushPress and Mindbody price per location). WellnessLiving prices by plan and staff count.

What each vendor says about boxing and kickboxing

  • PushPress has a boxing studio page written for fitness boxing and kickboxing studios. It lists online booking with a waiver signed before the first class (parents and guardians can sign for minors), intro offers and class packs next to memberships, class caps at your bag or station count with waitlists, appointment packages for 1:1 and small-group pad work, and a shop for gloves, wraps and drinks on the front desk tablet. Lead text-back and trial follow-up come with Grow, a $329/mo add-on.
  • Gymdesk published a boxing gym software guide, dated October 22, 2026, that ranks itself first. It says any class can carry a non-member drop-in price, class packs count down at check-in, and gloves can be sold with sizes as product variants. Its membership help page covers recurring, one-time, per-session and trial pricing.
  • TeamUp is general fitness studio software. Its features page lists memberships, class packs, drop-ins and pay-as-you-go options, booking rules for cancellations and class capacity, rentals of spaces in your gym, and payments through Stripe or GoCardless. Its blog features a Brooklyn boxing coach who uses it to book private sessions.
  • Zen Planner's membership page lists class packs, drop-ins, punch cards and family plans, all billed automatically. We found no boxing-specific page.
  • Wodify's pricing page lists online sales of memberships, packages, drop-ins and trials, spot booking, in-person retail and weekly attendance streaks on every plan. Lead automations start on Accelerate ($299/mo list).
  • RhinoFit has a boxing gym software page. It lists custom memberships billed automatically or one time, a product store with inventory, waivers, a class calendar for classes and individual sessions, email and SMS, and, as newer features, win/loss records, check-in access and product sales reporting.
  • Mindbody's help pages explain class pricing options (single, multiple, unlimited, autopay) and intro offers that a client can buy only once. Mindbody also charges 20% (capped at $30) on the first purchase of a new client who finds you through the Mindbody app.
  • WellnessLiving has a boxing and kickboxing article that recommends itself. Its pricing page lists intro offers for new clients, Book-a-Spot asset reservations, rewards and a leaderboard.
  • Spark Membership's kickboxing gym page says Spark works for studios without belt ranks. It lists rotating class formats on a shared calendar, automatic billing with failed-payment retries, a point of sale for gloves and wraps with inventory, two-way SMS for leads, digital waivers and reactivation campaigns for lapsed members.

Dojo Champ lists boxing among the disciplines on its MMA gym page and has one flat $199/mo plan, but it's built around martial arts schools; see our MMA gym software page.

Questions to ask in a demo

  1. If someone buys a drop-in or a 10-pack this month, do they count toward my price tier?
  2. Can a class pack expire, and can I limit it to certain classes?
  3. Can I stop the same person from buying the free intro class twice?
  4. Can I cap a class at my bag count, and can members pick a bag?
  5. Do PT and pad sessions come off a package automatically at check-in?
  6. What is the card rate, and is there a per-transaction fee on top?

Our software buying checklist has more demo questions. For intro-class booking and lead follow-up, see trial class booking software. For class-pack studios beyond combat sports, see class booking software for studios.

faq: What is the best software for a boxing or kickboxing gym?

We don't rank them. It depends on how you sell. PushPress, Gymdesk, TeamUp, Zen Planner, Wodify, RhinoFit and Mindbody all publish support for drop-ins and class packs. PushPress has a $0 plan, RhinoFit Standard is a flat $57/mo, and Gymdesk starts at $75/mo with Gymdesk Payments (prices checked November 28, 2026).
Does boxing gym software handle class packs and drop-ins?

Most do. PushPress, Gymdesk, TeamUp, Zen Planner, Wodify and Mindbody list both on their own pages, and RhinoFit lists class-limited and single-purchase memberships. Spark's kickboxing page doesn't mention packs or drop-ins, so ask Spark.
Do drop-in customers count toward active-member pricing?

It depends on the vendor. Gymdesk doesn't count visitors, frozen or cancelled members, or prospects. Zen Planner counts anyone with a membership or who attended in the past month. TeamUp counts anyone who booked or bought something in the month. PushPress, Wodify, RhinoFit Standard and Spark don't price by member count.
Can members pick a specific bag or spot?

Mindbody offers Pick-a-Spot on its Accelerate and Ultimate plans, WellnessLiving lists Book-a-Spot asset reservations, and Wodify lists spot booking on Essentials. PushPress lets you cap each class at your bag or station count with a waitlist.
Which tools have a free plan for a small boxing gym?
PushPress Free is $0/mo with a 4.99% + 30¢ card rate. RhinoFit Start Up is $0 for 20 or fewer active users, though RhinoFit says it may restrict payment processing and communications on that plan.
